text:
**For most buyers, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** All the sources agree on this.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles. NMC units are rated for roughly 500 to 1,000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily use, that is about 1.4 years for a 500-cycle NMC unit versus about 8 years for a 3,000-cycle LFP unit.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. One test had LFP peaking at 259°C against 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). It's not fireproof, though, and one study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner under overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One retailer database shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Most current mid-size and large models are LFP.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter, case, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about a 10% median difference ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some LFP units are even lighter per watt-hour than some NMC ones, so compare specific models.

**Things that don't depend on chemistry**
- **Cold weather:** Nearly all stations, LFP or NMC, refuse to charge below 32°F. Check each model's manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One site claims LFP handles cold better, but the others say it varies by maker.
- **Cycle ratings aren't always comparable:** Check the end point (70% vs. 80% capacity) and the warranty length.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Home backup or indoor storage:** LiFePO4.
- **Rare use with a strict weight limit:** either one. Compare the actual weights.
- **You already own a working NMC unit:** keep using it.
